name: Wilder Kaiser & Kaiserbachtal
kurzbeschreibung: The iconic Wilder Kaiser mountain range captivates with rugged limestone peaks, via ferratas, panoramic trails, and famous Bergdoktor film sets.
preis: Freely accessible; mountain cable cars require tickets (Kitzbüheler Alpen Sommer Card valid)
oeffnungszeiten: Hiking season late May to late October; cable cars run daily from 08:30 to 17:00
beschreibung:
Overview

The world-famous limestone massif of the Wilder Kaiser soars above the Tyrolean Unterland between Kufstein, St. Johann in Tirol, and the picturesque villages of Ellmau, Going, Scheffau, and Söll. Featuring jagged limestone pinnacles, sheer rock faces, and its highest summit, the Ellmauer Halt (2,344 m), the range is one of the most dramatic natural landmarks of the Northern Limestone Alps. Protected as a nature reserve since 1963, the Kaisergebirge preserves an unspoiled alpine wilderness. For generations, the Wilder Kaiser has been celebrated as the cradle of extreme free climbing, where alpine legends like Hans Dülfer and Hermann Buhl made mountaineering history. Today, the region combines world-class via ferratas, lush alpine pastures, and famous film settings into an internationally acclaimed holiday destination.

Route & Requirements

The Wilder Kaiser boasts an exemplary signposted trail network for every ability. Families and leisure hikers will enjoy sunny panoramic paths around the Rübezahl-Alm in Ellmau or the scenic circuit around the deep-blue Lake Hintersteiner See. Experienced mountain hikers can tackle the multi-day Kaiserkrone circuit that loops the entire massif in five stages. Those aiming for the rugged rocky peaks like the Totenkirchl or Ellmauer Halt require extensive alpine experience, absolute surefootedness, a head for heights, and a climbing helmet. A certified via ferrata kit is mandatory on challenging secured routes like the Kaiseregg or Jubiläumssteig. Ankle-high hiking boots and rain gear are essential on rocky terrain. Cosy alpine huts along the routes provide welcoming shelter.

Visit & Arrival

The hiking season runs from late May to late October. The Kaiser villages are served by modern mountain railways (accepted on the Kitzbüheler Alpen Sommer Card). Rail passengers travel to Kufstein, Wörgl, or St. Johann in Tirol; free Kaiserjet shuttle buses connect villages and trailheads frequently. Drivers take the A12 Inntal motorway (exit Kufstein Süd or Wörgl Ost) and B178 directly into the Kaiser region.

Tips

Visit the filming locations of 'Der Bergdoktor' in Ellmau and take in the view of the imposing Kaiserkrone. A hike up to the rustic Gruttenhütte at 1,599 meters rewards you with hearty dumplings and a breathtaking vista extending across the Kitzbühel Alps to the High Tauern.
saison: Mai bis Oktober (Winterwandern im Tal möglich)
